title: Eigenvalues of multipartite entanglement witnesses
abstract: We investigate various properties of multipartite block-positive operators, decomposable EWs (DEWs), and non-decomposable EWs. We provide a necessary and sufficient condition to construct a special DEW using the multipartite GHZ state. For multipartite DEW, we explicitly characterize the supremum and infimum of maximum and minimum eigenvalues, as well as the trace of its square. We also derive other results concerning NDEW, eigenvalues of $2 \times n$ EWs and the corresponding physical implications. Furthermore, we investigate the tightness of inequalities of these eigenvalues with examples.
summary: This paper mathematically characterizes entanglement witnesses (EWs) in multipartite quantum systems, distinguishing between decomposable and non-decomposable types. It derives necessary and sufficient conditions and establishes precise bounds on the eigenvalues and spectral properties of these witnesses. This work provides rigorous tools for quantifying entanglement detection in complex quantum states.
main_problem: The paper investigates the mathematical properties of entanglement witnesses (EWs) in multipartite quantum systems, specifically classifying them as decomposable (DEWs) or non-decomposable (NDEW).
main_result: The authors provide necessary and sufficient conditions for constructing special DEWs using the GHZ state and explicitly characterize the bounds (supremum/infimum) for key spectral properties like eigenvalues and the trace of the square of the witness.
method: The analysis relies heavily on linear algebra, decomposing the EW operator into blocks based on subspace splittings, and deriving rigorous inequalities for the eigenvalues.
model_or_system: The focus is on multipartite quantum systems (up to n-qubit systems) and the mathematical tools used to detect entanglement, represented by the entanglement witness operator W.
key_observables: Eigenvalues of the EW ($\lambda_k$), the trace of the square of the witness ($	ext{Tr}(W^2)$), and the expectation value $	ext{Tr}(Who)$ used for entanglement detection.
important_parameters: The dimensionality of the system ($n$-qubits) and the specific structure of the witness (e.g., $2 	imes n$ EWs).
main_assumptions: The analysis builds upon the definitions of DEWs and NDEWs, and in some sections, assumes the existence of a genuine 2 $	imes$ n EW to constrain the operator structure.
figures_summary: Table I summarizes eigenvalue ranges for $2 	imes n$ EWs, while Table II summarizes bounds for DEWs and NDEWs regarding $	ext{Tr}(W^2)$ and specific eigenvalues.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from general properties of block-positive operators to specific characterizations of DEWs and NDEWs, culminating in detailed eigenvalue results for $2 	imes n$ systems and general multipartite systems.
why_interesting: The rigorous mathematical characterization of entanglement witnesses provides concrete, quantifiable thresholds for detecting entanglement in complex, multi-partite quantum states, which is fundamental to quantum information theory.
